newsitem.title: USA: U.S. pork exports may rise due to Taiwan ban.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pork exports may rise due to Taiwan ban.

text.p: U.S. pork exports may increase as a result of Taiwan's ban on its pork exports, Chris Goldthwait, general sales manager for the Agriculture Department said Friday.
"It would seem there would be some commercial opportunities for our pork exports into traditional Taiwan pork markets," Goldthwait told Reuters.
Goldthwait said it was not surprising if Taiwan is reducing its corn imports, but said an uptick in U.S. pork shipments could help offset the loss of corn and soybean exports to Taiwan.
The Taiwan Council of Agriculture announced Thursday that it was banning all exports of fresh and frozen pork temporarily due to an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease there.
Pork is one of Taiwan's biggest export items. Taiwan provides 45 percent of Japan's pork imports, while the U.S. accounts for 23 percent of Japan's pork purchases.
Taiwan is a major customer for U.S. farm products and was the number three buyer of U.S. corn and soybeans last year.
Some estimates are that Taiwan's corn imports could drop by 20 percent because of the ban.
Taiwan overnight passed on a tender for 112,000 tonnes of U.S. or Argentine corn. Commenting on this, Goldthwait said, "Under the circumstances, it's not too surprising."
Goldthwait, however, was careful in how much he speculated on the long-term impact of the Taiwan pork export ban, saying it would depend on how long the ban was in place.
"At this point, I do not know the seriousness of the situation," Goldthwait said. But he noted that Taiwan is one of the most important agricultural customers of the United States.
